Shri Ramachandra hearing the humble and piteous words 
of Shri Sita, unwilling to let the princess accompany him, 
sought to dissuade her by describing the hardships of a forest 
life.

hardships to be borne in the forest, in spite of Sita's entreaty 
was unwilling to grant her request. 
Once more, he addressed the weeping Sita, insisting she 
should not accompany him, saying : " 0 Sita, thou art nobly 
born and devoted to the practice of virtue ; remain here 
continuing to act righteously. 0 Frail Princess, act according

relinquish the thought of sharing my elile, many are the dangers

human habitation. For thine own well-being, I advise thee

brief.summary_1line: Rama gently refuses Sita’s plea to accompany him, describing the many hardships and dangers of forest life to persuade her to remain in Ayodhya.

image_candidates.scene_text: Rama speaks solemnly to the tearful Sita in the palace, describing the terrifying forest of roaring lions, snakes, and thorny paths.
A vision of the wild forest Rama describes: dark caves with roaring lions, tangled thorns, storm clouds, and serpents coiling near a river.
